steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Shamare, the others are going to diagnose and treat the Infected patients in the ward. Will you be okay here by yourself?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Err, I mean... Morte will keep you company, so the two of you will be fine, right?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: ...Mm. You go and take care of them. I can handle things here.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: 'Handle'? I wasn't giving you an assignment...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Well, whatever. Shamare is pretty mature compared to some of the other children at Rhodes Island, so I'll just trust her.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Alright, I'll get started with work then.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, you heard that sound too, didn't you?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mhm. I know, you'd recognize the sound of crying anywhere.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Signor Mauro, please don't do this. It'll only make things harder for me.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: As an Infected, if your insurance payment falls below half of the designated amount, you can no longer continue to work.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: B-But I already made a full payment... Yesterday, last night, your subordinates came by to collect it!

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: My subordinates? I didn't arrange for that, nor have I seen any of this supposed payment.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Look, it's written clearly in the code here that insurance money is to be collected by the judge.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: It's your responsibility to make sure the money gets to me. Otherwise, how would I know to update the records?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: And I'm sorry, but according to the records, you're currently delinquent in your payments.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: But they... Last time they came around, they said, 'there's no way a judge would go around personally collecting debts'...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Take another good look at this codex, and think back carefully. Are you sure you're remembering right?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Oh, uhh... I'm so sorry, I seem to have misremembered. Pardon my foolishness, Your Honor.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: But that doesn't change the fact that I don't have a single centesimo to pay...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Is that so? What a pity. You're in no shape to accept the work we offer either.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Therefore, according to the law, my only option is to confiscate a piece of your property as collateral.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: I-I don't even have anything left worth that much...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Oh? Are you implying that you're a better appraiser of value than I am?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: But my family can't survive without food! P-Please, I beg of you... Just give me a little more time!

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: I swear, I'll find some way to get the money.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: I only ask you to respect the rule of law. Understood?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...Yes, of course.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: And by sheer coincidence, there happens to be something of value right in front of me, which the law allows you to offer up as collateral.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: D-Do you mean this pocket watch here?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...Oh, you're absolutely right! I can't believe I forgot!

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: As long as you remember now.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Now then, let's agree to meet again when the hour hand of this watch makes two full circuits.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Oh, thank you for your magnanimity...

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Then, according to the law, can get it back after I pay? Th-That's a keepsake from my great-grandfather's time in the famiglia's civil war... and it allows me some semblance of respect.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, should we go talk to that lady? ...Hm, it's better if we stay quiet?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: There are already a bunch of curses following her. Something bad's gonna happen unless we do something.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Hmm? What an unkempt child, running about all by herself...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Are you looking for your family?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Perhaps you should search a trash can in a back alley, the bottom of the river, the cemetery, or the garden... I'm sure they'd be somewhere like that.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Does it hurt, Morte? ...It's raining, but it's not hurting from the rain.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: She'll also be in unbearable pain.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: (What the hell did that girl just say?)

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...Damnit, this rain's giving me a headache. Let's not worry about it.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: The Messenger just arrived, and these are all for you.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Did a postcard from Volsinii come in?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: I wouldn't dare read your mail without permission.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: But you've done so much good work, I'm sure you'll receive the praise of the head... Dare I say, the postcard should already be on its way.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Mm. Let's look through the other ones first.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: A gift from the boss of the paper mill, and compensation from twenty households on East Street. Not bad.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: An invitation from the town council? Why would I need this?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: And a plea from their son in prison... Rubbish.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...Wait, hold on.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: There's something written on the back?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Come here. I have a job for you.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: ...You're letting that criminal out? But his famiglia hasn't coughed up the dough yet.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Take a look at the back side.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: It's just a blank piece of paper...

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: *cough* Oh, of course. It's gotta mean the sender is going to be disposed of cleanly, without leaving any traces.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: While the very idea of using curses to vent your grievances is laughable, I don't want to see anyone trampling over my code of law.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Curses? What?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Alright, onto the next letter.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: —What's going on here?!

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: You, come back. Hand me that letter.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: If you say so.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...The exact same contents and handwriting.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Every letter! It's on every single letter!

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: 'Your malice has brought about a curse, and calamity shall follow in your wake. The black fowlbeast circles, and you will lose the only glittering thing on you.'

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...How juvenile.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Find out whose childish prank this is.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: But, it's just a blank sheet of paper.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: I mean... On it, boss! We'll find this prankster.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Still no leads on those 'cursed' letters from yesterday? How many people could there possibly be in this tiny little town?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Tch, maybe I need to find myself some more capable subordinates?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...The pocket watch I took from that Infected is running five minutes slow.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: I must say, I am tolerant to a fault.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: I can only hope he doesn't betray that compassion.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Sir, do you remember when you first developed symptoms of Oripathy?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: I... I'm not sure. Maybe a few days ago?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: To the best of your knowledge, do you have any clue how you might have contracted it?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: To be frank, based on our preliminary screening, you, like many others here, recently came down with an acute infection.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: We need to locate the source of the epidemic to try to contain the spread of Oripathy in town.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Umm, I'm not quite following.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: I-I used to work in the back kitchen of that restaurant over there, that's all I know. Seriously, I don't know a thing.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Alright. Sorry for bothering you then.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Shamare, did you notice anything unusual over there? Like, have you felt the effects of active Originium, or lost control of your Arts like before?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Shamare? What are you looking at?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: ...Black fowlbeast.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Who are you people? What are you here for?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Oh, hello there. We're a medical organization, and we're working with the town hospital to provide some technical support.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: So, you're from Columbia?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Not quite...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: In any case, I need to talk to this gentleman here. Now, if you'll excuse me—

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: —Gah! A fowlbeast?!

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Shoo! Go away! Stop pecking me!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Oh, she dropped her pocket watch...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: ...What are you tugging on my sleeve for?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Wait here. Don't move.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: *cough*, *cough, cough*... Tch, the damn thing finally flew off.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: But a black fowlbeast...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Hah, how could someone put a curse on me?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Your Honor, I... Um, is there anything I can do for? Do you need me to tidy up your clothes?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: No, I simply want to see the law upheld.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Oh, of course, you're here for the insurance money... Here you go.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: This isn't enough.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: But... You haven't even counted it yet.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: The envelope should be at least three times as thick. Did you not remember to include the late fees?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Look, it's written right here in the codex. That's the law. My hands are tied.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...I see, I must have remembered wrong. I'll try looking for somewhere else to borrow money, so please, give me a little more time.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Of course. I am nothing if not tolerant.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: (Where'd that beat-up gold pocket watch go? Did I drop it somewhere?)

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: (The curse... No, this was just a coincidence. How could anyone believe in curses?)

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...In any case, I'll see you again in two days.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Damn my luck! Fine, if that's what it takes, then so be it!

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: You accursed eyeless fowlbeast! It's all your fault! If she weren't in such a bad mood just now, this whole thing would already be settled!

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, could you pick up the pocket watch?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mm. It didn't break when it fell.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Here, this is yours.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (I knew it, Shamare used her Originium Arts. We could all see it fall to the ground, but somehow the judge didn't notice.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Has she already matured to the point where she's this considerate of others?)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Does she even realize how incredibly brave that was just now?)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (...But even with all the Arts training she's had at Rhodes Island, casting something like that must be stressful on her body.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Anyway, she might be doing the right thing, but I'll need to keep a closer eye on her condition... and help her out if necessary.)

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: It represents 'famiglia' to you. 'A very big family.' It's important, right?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Do you not want it back?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...What are you talking about? Th-That isn't mine.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: I've never seen it in my life. Do whatever you want with it, since I've certainly never seen it before! And I definitely didn't see it today!

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: ...Really?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're pretty energetic today, Morte.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: What'd you eat? Sadness? Fear? Or resentment?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Why are you afraid? I wanna know too.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: J-Just turn around and leave with that pocket watch! I'm shutting the door!

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: But I still wanna know.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Obviously there's not a single word written in that lady's book.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: So why didn't you tell her?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...Anyone can see it's a legal codex; how could there be no words written in it? I bet you don't know how to read anyway.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Hey, you, the doctor over there! Aren't you an adult? Take this crazy kid away from me! Get away from me and my house!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Let's go, Shamare.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Everything's been smooth sailing today. No cases in need of a hearing.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Only minor stuff on the streets too. Someone ran into a mugger while eating at a restaurant, but they turned out to be one of the recently Infected who hasn't paid their dues.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Which ensures we're getting our money on time.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Yup. Also...

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: It seems a lot of folks have been talking about you behind your back.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Talking? About what?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Some crazy 'prophecies' scribbled on posters in the alleys.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: I sent some people to find who did it, but no luck. All the posters should be taken down by now though.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: What, are there still people out there who haven't learned to respect the will of the law?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: So, who are these people who've been gossiping about this instead of reporting it to me?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: About that... I haven't heard of anyone actually talking about it.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: You're contradicting yourself. If nobody's talking about it, then how are they talking about it?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: ...Same way as always.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: They keep quiet, but you can see it in their eyes.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: One look at their shifty gazes, and you know the score.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: What are you thinking? Shamare and I were just enjoying a meal when you walked over. You were patting your two children on the head just now...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Frankly, I thought you were coming in to order two kids' meals for them.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Turns out, you're trying to rob us?!

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: This is just how we do things, outsider!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Stop struggling. Shamare and I won't let you cause any trouble. This is how we do things.

spans.text: Stop struggling. Shamare and I won't let you cause any trouble. This is how

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Hah... Weren't you guys there yesterday? Didn't you see how much insurance money I owed?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: If you actually care whether we Infected live or die, then put your money where your mouth is and don't stop me!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I might not fully understand your circumstances, but I do know that what comes around goes around.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Look, your two kids are still playing with the other kids out on the street. If you make a customer here bleed, what do you think is going to happen to them next?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...Then tell me, what should I do?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: If they end up kicking me and my family out of the house, what else is there for me to think about?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: ...That won't happen.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte will help.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mortw will help me find more.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The soil here is already full of resentment and fear. I just need a few other things.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Uh, don't worry about it. I'll help her help you.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Help me? What can you people possibly do?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Sometimes, when a person is tormented by malice so thick that it completely engulfs them, their mind can jump to the craziest things—even hallucinations. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Just don't cause any trouble for me like last time.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: ...Oh right, Signor Mauro, we'd like to schedule an appointment with you.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: If that woman claiming to be a judge doesn't come by tomorrow to collect your debt, we'd like to ask you a bit more about the large number of Infected here. Can you do that?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: 'Your malice has brought a curse upon you'... The same as last time.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Hah, utter nonsense.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: For sure. How could anyone take a prank like this seriously?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: We're still looking for whoever's behind this garbage, but... Well, the hard part is, none of us have ever seen this 'cursed text' ourselves.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: We've managed to piece together the contents, but nobody seems to know who left it behind... Or at least, nobody's telling us anything.
She realizes that the pedestrians along the street are avoiding her gaze, but nevertheless seem curious and inquisitive as they walk past her.
Silence is a form of order, but at the moment, she finds their silence terrifying.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: ...Tch.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: I don't feel like wasting any time on that Infected today. If he doesn't come up with the money, just confiscate his house.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: This is the last time I'll—

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Urgh!

a.text: 'Your malice has brought a curse upon you. The soil here is unwilling to bear your weight any longer, and the evil spirits that linger shall make you fall so hard that you will be unable to walk again.'

steps.text: The moment she falls to the ground, the curse she'd heard echoes through the judge's mind.
A sharp pain shoots through her calf, and she hears whispers from the side of the road.

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: A-Are you alright? I'll help you up. There are too many people staring; it'll ruin your image...

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Get away from me!

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: If you say so.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Damn it all... Are you blind?! I'm hurt! Take me to the hospital!

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Uhh, okay...

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Want me to have someone else deal with that Infected? It's not exactly a big deal.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: If this keeps up, will this curse never leave me?

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Err... Since when are curses real?

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Do you not see it?! It's as real as anything! It's chasing after me! The evil spirits are after me!

steps.name: Judge's Subordinate
steps.text: Just calm down, ma'am... Everyone's looking at us.

steps.name: Town Judge
steps.text: Anyway, don't worry about that Infected for now. I need to calm myself first.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Well, as promised, I'll tell you what I know.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: To be blunt, you're wasting your time here. There's no underground Originium mine like you might've guessed, or a big scary factory either.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: All that happened was some gang war that lasted about a month, and a lot of us were unlucky enough to get caught in the crossfire. That's all there is to it.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: By the way, I've heard that there's been quite a bit of Originium smuggling going on...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: If the gangsters used it to make explosives, and didn't follow safety standards during production, it'd be easy for active Originium dust to leak out.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: It's also very common for those who get infected to not notice their physical symptoms at first. Or worse, hide them. This can create the false impression that new patients are still appearing.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Nobody's stupid enough to tell a doctor that they got infected in a gang war.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: They'll just pretend they didn't see anything.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But if there was such large-scale, open conflict going on, why didn't the judges put a stop to it?

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Judges? Haha, I don't know how they do things in the big city, but there are no judges out in the boonies.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: The gangsters were backed by different famiglie, and they fought until one side drove the other completely out of town and took control.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: The 'judge' you met earlier was just an ordinary mafiosa used by the winning famiglia to control us here.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Ugh... Sorry, I really only intended to ask about the Oripathy.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Thank you for helping us complete our mission.

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: Haha, I should be thanking you, if only for pushing my bad luck back one day...

spans.text: , if only for pushing my bad luck back one day...

steps.name: Mauro, Infected Citizen
steps.text: That said, your little girl here doesn't seem to want my thanks.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Don't worry about her. She tends to space out, but I'm sure she heard what you said.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: One more thing, after you head back, remember to take this medicine to control your condition. Take care.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Shamare.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I told you, Morte would help him. Why didn't you believe me?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: No, that's not what I meant. Actually, you've already done too much, for too many people.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: The next time you use your Originium Arts, make sure you discuss it with us first.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: If you'd lost control doing what you did, you could've hurt other people very badly... maybe even yourself.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: They always tell me that back at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: As long as Morte doesn't get hurt, it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: And you always say that. As long as Morte is in good spirits, as long as Morte doesn't get hurt, it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But the truth is, I can tell you're already extremely worn out. I can't let that build up to the point where it affects your health.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I won't use any more Arts here.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Also... Give me another apple. Not the Arts Unit.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I want something to eat.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Haha, sure.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: We've confirmed the source of the infection here, and now that we've finished our emergency treatment for the remaining Infected, it's time we headed back to the landship.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Packed up all your tools? If there's nothing else, be ready to pull out.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: My apologies. Everyone, pull your carts over and let the disabled woman through.

steps.name: Town 'Judge'
steps.text: ...Is your investigation over? I heard that your company was looking into the cause of all these infections. Did you get your results?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Ah, about that...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: The time we have on these business trips is extremely limited, and unfortunately we were unable to determine a single cause of the outbreak. Our sincerest apologies.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Go get her book for me.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (For some, being thrust into an environment that reminds them of the past would only stir up the pain buried deep in their hearts... But maybe, for Shamare, that was never a problem to begin with.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Though it's hardly normal, she is indeed growing in her own way.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Um, Shamare, I have to praise you for having the composure to do what you did.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Huh? What do you mean?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: The reason you used your Arts is probably because you—Or rather, because Morte felt a pain from this town similar to the pain it knew from before.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: People treat each other with malice, and vent those emotions at one another.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: And even though so many people knew that you weren't the source of the curse, and that you were completely innocent... nobody was willing to those words out loud.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: So in this small town, you used your Arts to help everyone speak out, including the Infected.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: 'There are no words in that codex.'

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: You've grown so much I'm almost astounded.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're... weird.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte doesn't need to think about complicated stuff like that, so I don't either.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte just wanted to eat that judge's emotions, so I fed it. Isn't that all there is to it?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I see. So you didn't put that much thought into it, huh?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: And I spent so long mulling it over before finally authorizing you to use your Originium Arts...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But I guess in the end, I only felt like she was being a bully and had to be punished... I suppose simple reasons like that can be fine too.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: —Hey, hold on, the thought that maybe I don't need to lecture you for this just suddenly popped into my head... Don't tell me that was another one of your 'spiritual suggestions'?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: And why are you smiling?

steps.name: 'Judge's' Subordinate
steps.text: I brought your crutches.

steps.name: Town 'Judge'
steps.text: Alright. I'm going to rest for now. I'll let you know if I need anything later.

steps.name: 'Judge's' Subordinate
steps.text: Gotcha.

steps.name: Town 'Judge'
steps.text: Phew... I haven't heard of any more curses these last few days, so maybe this nightmare is finally ending.

steps.name: Town 'Judge'
steps.text: What a pleasant Sunday morning. Now that the rain has passed, the air feels fresher than usual.

steps.name: Town 'Judge'
steps.text: Hmm?
The legal codex she had offhandedly placed on the table is blown to a new page by a gust of wind.
Fwoosh, fwoosh.
She sees a line of writing on it. A line with the same handwriting as the curse from before.

a.text: 'You will see these words on a Sunday morning, and shall incur a curse.'
'You shall tremble in fear before the consequences of your malice, and decide to change your evil ways.'
